title: Types
description:
## Types
Types are what Haskell is. Haskell would be NOTHING without types. There are a few core types in Haskell:
- Int: A whole number
- Double: A decimal number.
- Word: A non-negative whole number
- Bool: True or False
- Char: A single character wrapped in ''
- String: A string of text wrapped in ""
(): `()` represents nothing meaningfull
- IO: A special type that represents actions which interact with the outside world. It wraps another type, like `IO String` or `IO Int`, meaning "a result produced by a side effect."
